sources.title: Gravity versus magnetics over basin-fill faults
sources.excerpt: The aeromagnetic data did not provide any insight into the response of the minor faults but rather served to verify the regional response of the whole profile.
sources.supports: Gravity/magnetic responses need not both resolve a minor fault; supports testing independent per-field signed profiles rather than requiring magnetic corroboration.
sources.limits: Arizona case study, not a Great Basin validation or proof that our curvature transform improves DTI.

sources.title: Aeromagnetic expressions of concealed faults
sources.excerpt: The horizontal gradient method applied to reduced-to-pole aeromagnetic data is particularly effective in mapping fault locations, especially at regional scales.
sources.supports: Juxtaposed differing strata can produce magnetic fault signatures; anomaly shape varies with depth/thickness/susceptibility; RTP gradients can aid interpretation.
sources.limits: Rio Grande rift examples; nonfault contacts, remanence and topography remain competing explanations. Does not establish our forecast or pinpoint blind faults here.
sources.verification: Read complete official USGS record on 2026-10-01; DOI 10.1130/GES00128.1.

sources.title: Radiometric interpretation and survey-boundary confounders
sources.excerpt: Care should be taken when interpreting the patterns on these maps to avoid attaching geologic significance to boundaries between surveys.
sources.supports: Radiometric composition/ratios may indicate lithology, alteration or weathering; survey-boundary offsets are a non-geological competing explanation.
sources.limits: Alaska NURE, not GeoDAWN. Its flight spacing, penetration/resolution and typical ratio figures are NOT adopted as GeoDAWN metadata. Pinned uint8 channel ranks do not recover physical K/Th units.
